statement: At matched six-sample receptive field the staple associator carries nonzero but small information beyond the geometric baselines: on the deduplicated THEMIS-A Staples benchmark (23,664,374 samples, 578,320 positives, 813 daily files), a logistic model on ln(dbdt), ln(rot), ln(cumrot6), ln(maxrot6), ln(pvi6), ln(gram6) reaches out-of-fold ROC-AUC 0.8428 under 5-fold file-grouped cross-validation, adding ln(assoc) raises it to 0.8448, and the paired bootstrap over 1000 file resamples (ChaCha8 seed 42) gives delta ROC-AUC +0.0020 [0.0017, 0.0023], delta PR-AUC +0.0005 [0.0001, 0.0008] and delta log loss -0.00012 [-0.00018, -0.00007], every interval excluding zero in the associator's favor. The unique contribution is 0.2 percent of AUC, an order of magnitude below the standalone margins C-1631 reports, so the associator's standalone discrimination is mostly redundant with six-sample angular and magnitude statistics and not entirely so.

Under a fixed linear-in-log-features logistic model (ridge 1e-6, Newton-Raphson, standardization fitted inside each training fold) with a fixed 5-fold assignment grouped by daily file (one ChaCha8 seed-42 shuffle), adding ln(assoc) to the six matched six-sample baselines ln(dbdt), ln(rot), ln(cumrot6), ln(maxrot6), ln(pvi6), ln(gram6) raises out-of-fold ROC-AUC on the deduplicated THEMIS-A Staples benchmark (23,664,374 samples, 578,320 positives, 813 daily files) from 0.8428 to 0.8448, an incremental predictive discrimination of +0.20 AUC percentage points with paired file-bootstrap 95 percent interval [+0.17, +0.23] over 1000 resamples and zero adverse resamples; PR-AUC rises by +0.05 percentage points [+0.01, +0.08] and log loss falls by 0.00012 [0.00007, 0.00018]. Every interval excludes zero in the associator's favor, and the increment is about 0.24 percent of the baseline AUC, an order of magnitude below the standalone margins C-1631 reports. The statement is about incremental discrimination under this model class and fold assignment, not about information-theoretic uniqueness.

On the retained deduplicated THEMIS-A Staples crossing-day sample-localization benchmark (23,664,374 time points, 578,320 positives, 813 daily files), the normalized 16D staple-associator has pooled ROC-AUC 0.827449 with file-cluster-bootstrap 95 percent interval [0.820525, 0.834788]. It exceeds the implemented PVI and Gram-volume controls across the bulk and both predeclared gradient strata: simultaneous assoc-minus-PVI margin 0.043572 [0.036509, 0.050594] and assoc-minus-Gram margin 0.021609 [0.018430, 0.024935], from 2,000 intact-file resamples at seed 42. The associator and Gram statistic consume six local samples. PVI takes the maximum increment from those six samples and divides by the RMS increment of the complete daily file, including later samples. The comparison establishes superiority over these offline implementations; the PVI comparison includes unequal calibration context.

On the retained deduplicated THEMIS-A Staples benchmark (23,664,374 samples, 578,320 positives, 813 daily files), adding ln(assoc) to a fixed logistic model on ln(dbdt), ln(rot), ln(cumrot6), ln(maxrot6), ln(pvi6), and ln(gram6) raises out-of-fold ROC-AUC from 0.8428282833 to 0.8448147157. The model uses ridge 1e-6, Newton-Raphson fitting, training-fold standardization, and one five-fold daily-file-grouped seed-42 assignment. The dbdt and rot features use two samples; cumrot6 and maxrot6 and gram6 use six; pvi6 uses a six-sample increment numerator with complete daily-file RMS calibration. A paired bootstrap of 1,000 file resamples of the frozen out-of-fold predictions gives a delta ROC-AUC interval [0.0016817229, 0.0023033193], with zero adverse ROC-AUC resamples. Delta PR-AUC has interval [0.0000948498, 0.0008139584], with five adverse resamples; delta log loss has interval [-0.0001824100, -0.0000688957]. The result measures incremental predictive discrimination for this offline feature set, model, and fold assignment; its uncertainty excludes variation from repeated model fitting.

On 23,456,246 warmup-filtered THEMIS-A benchmark rows (574,716 positives, 813 files), adding logged staple-associator magnitude to the fixed six-feature ridge-logistic baseline yields positive pooled out-of-fold ROC-AUC increments in every one of five file-grouped five-fold assignments (seeds 42 through 46): daily-file RMS 0.0020033257278800898 to 0.0020158658710166533, training-file RMS 0.002394591060060347 to 0.002422900809169848, and preceding-256-increment RMS 0.0033726281856922835 to 0.0034006522849118204. Across 100 paired whole-train-file and whole-test-file bootstrap draws in the fixed seed-42 fold-0 partition, with RMS, standardization, and both models refitted in each arm and draw, the minimum incremental ROC-AUC across all three arms has median 0.0017528829999793327 and linear 2.5/97.5 percentile interval [0.0010345135981383064, 0.002696001071597234]. All 100 minima are positive, and all 750 planned fits converge. The CV ranges describe correlated split sensitivity; the interval supports a positive predictive increment only under the declared conditional procedure.
status_note: Map counting convention: count each named feature-construction or model-transformation stage once along a branch, including a fitted transform as one stage; shared branches are reported separately rather than summed. These computational stage counts are declared bookkeeping, not phenomenological interpretive depth or evidence of a physical algebra-to-observable derivation. Associator score has 4 ordered maps: (1) augment each magnetic vector with its Euclidean magnitude; (2) pack four consecutive augmented vectors into R16, taking three overlapping staples over k..k+5; (3) compute the Euclidean norm of the 16D Cayley-Dickson associator (ab)c-a(bc); (4) divide by the product of the three staple norms plus 1e-30. PVI score has 4 ordered stages: (1) lag-one vector-increment norms; (2) maximum of five increments spanning k..k+5; (3) estimate the denominator RMS from daily-file increments, pooled training-file increments, or 256 preceding input-row increments; (4) divide that maximum by the arm-specific RMS. RMS estimation is a parallel calibration branch entering stage 4. Equal timestamps restrict the rolling arm to input-row precedence. Each model branch adds 3 maps: (1) ln(score+1e-12) with f32 storage; (2) training-fitted mean/population-standard-deviation standardization; (3) fixed-ridge logistic fitting and f64 prediction. Thus the associator-to-model branch has 7 stages and the calibrated PVI-to-model branch has 7 stages. The other baseline branches are: dbdt, 2 stages (field magnitude, absolute k+3/k+4 magnitude difference without time division); rot, 1 stage (clamped normalized-dot-product angle at k+3/k+4); cumrot6 and maxrot6, 2 stages each (five consecutive angles over six samples, sum or maximum); gram6, 3 stages (five vector increments, absolute determinant of each consecutive increment triple, maximum). Adding the same 3 model maps gives respective branch counts 5, 4, 5, 5 and 6. Every grouped split and bootstrap draw refits RMS where training-defined, standardization, and both models. Evaluation maps are recorded separately from score construction: retain the common k>=256 warmup population; label k+4 within two minutes of a catalog crossing while feature availability reaches k+5; form descriptive gradient strata from the common-population positive dbdt median; split by whole file with seeds 42..46; resample whole training and test files in 100 paired draws on seed-42 fold-0; compute ROC-AUC, differences, the declared global minimum and linear 2.5/97.5 percentile endpoints. These conditional empirical comparisons establish neither streaming/precursor performance nor a physical interpretation of the embedding.

statement: On the timestamp-causal THEMIS-A crossing-day archive (22,263,526 admitted decisions, 543,911 positives, 813 daily files), training-only preprocessing and ridge-logistic fits on 2007-2012 produce a small positive canonical-associator increment over six matched geometric predictors in held-out 2015 and 2016. Across 2,000 paired whole-daily-file bootstrap draws, the global minimum ROC-AUC increment over calibration widths 64, 256 and 1024 and both final years has approximate 95 percent interval [0.0010149049086891153, 0.0029188809429172872]. The upper endpoint lies below the historical investigator-declared 0.005 discrimination target. The target has no established application-based justification; the below-target comparison leaves the positive-effect observation intact and practical utility unassessed. Fourteen to sixteen of nineteen exact-support sign controls equal or exceed canonical point ROC-AUC in every final panel; a declared post-hoc 120-contrast whole-file bootstrap comparison now finds 47 control-superiority intervals and 73 directionally inconclusive intervals, including all six matched-capacity geometric comparisons. Canonical superiority is unestablished; practical equivalence requires a declared margin. E-283 retains the native provider-product chronology failure. The separately declared retrospective external replication is reported by C-1754.

On the admitted THEMIS-A final 2015/2016 archive, a declared post-hoc paired whole-daily-file bootstrap with 2000 draws and simultaneous 95 percent intervals across 120 canonical-minus-control ROC-AUC contrasts yields 47 control-superiority intervals, 73 intervals crossing zero, and zero canonical-superiority intervals. The family includes nineteen exact-support sign controls and one matched geometric-capacity control at widths 64, 256 and 1024 in each year. All six geometric intervals cross zero. Algebra-specific superiority is unestablished; practical equivalence is unadjudicated without a declared margin. The result conditions on frozen fits, admits no external replication, and retains the separate historical 0.005 discrimination target for the baseline comparison. That target has no established application-based justification and supplies neither a general scientific gate nor a practical-utility verdict.

On all 166 THEMIS-D V2 crossing dates in 2015/2016, retrospective timestamp-only quarantine replaces four ambiguous timestamp fields while preserving original bytes by inverse reconstruction. The unchanged causal runner admits 4,219,790 decisions with 124,834 positives and evaluates 63 frozen THEMIS-A models with zero new training fits. Across 2,000 paired daily-file bootstrap draws, the global minimum canonical-associator ROC-AUC increment over the six-feature baseline across widths 64, 256 and 1024 and both years has approximate 95 percent interval [0.0007173048330896048, 0.0024898116600369224]. The interval supports a small positive external archive-conditional increment and lies below the historical investigator-declared 0.005 discrimination target. The target has no established application-based justification; the below-target comparison leaves practical utility unassessed. Independent support checks exclude quarantined rows and pre-reset history. Whole-file quality selection uses lookahead; online availability and ordinary-day false alerts remain unmeasured. E-283 retains its failed provider-product admission.
